q1_issues.issue: `vertical_expression` and `horizontal_desire` are fused as compound kinds, but neither adjective+noun pair names a recognized subtype (no term of art, origin adjective, role title or material adjective) — they are ad-hoc figurative description, which the compound section says must stay two atoms.

"the vertical expression **of** a horizontal desire" is the content argument of an action nominalization, not a genuinely possessive of-phrase, so `Possession` mis-encodes it — it is the excluded "a photo of Mary" case rather than "the engine of the car".

"legalized by music" is a participial post-modifier on the noun, i.e. a reduced relative clause, which the instruction set requires to be reified as an ordinary event with `music` as the `by`-phrase `Agent` — never as a relation named after the participle.

q2_gaps: verbless definitional apposition ("Dancing: <predicate nominal>") — the copular section covers only an overt "X is a/an N" / "X is ADJ", with nothing on a colon-linked definition

an of-phrase serving as the argument of an action/event nominalization ("the expression of a desire") — the genitive rules enumerate possession, partitive, measure and about-phrases, but give no form for a deverbal noun's own complement
notes: Conditional on the (questionable) fusion, the genus and adjectival-modifier decomposition atoms are emitted correctly, and `music` rightly stays a bare mass constant. The instruction set also says nothing about metaphorical predication, which is what the whole predicate nominal here is.
